analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE excerpts of .github/workflows/release-provider.yml (lines 1–1246), the complete changed-range map and bounded patch. The visible patch changes the documented caller contract from master-driven dev/staging lanes and a self-signed dev branch to a dev-branch caller using Developer ID signing. This affects release credentials and artifact identity (A-005, A-011, A-017; T-013, T-034, T-054), but comments alone do not prove an authorization regression.
BASE controls include master-policy source verification before resolving lanes (127–153), verified-source checkouts and build/qualification dependency gates (173–247), unsigned artifact/source/version validation before certificate import (347–394), profile and entitlement checks, hardened signing, notarization and final archived signature checks (396–859). Publication binds retained artifact IDs/digests and payload/provenance hashes across staging and serialized registration (919–1186). The privileged fan helper remains separately signed and dormant, with final identity/layout checks (555–565, 803–819), relevant to TB-010 and T-044–T-047. No supplied change demonstrates altered prompt encryption, cache isolation, token custody, billing or serving authorization.
No finding is supported because HEAD source for executable changed ranges is absent and the patch stops in comments. Integration must examine HEAD lines 142–145, 158–160 and 829–834, plus the changed callers and source/resume policy, to confirm which dev revisions may consume signing credentials, how reviewed-source authorization now works, and whether final artifact verification remains intact. Reconcile artifact provenance and environment separation with publication policy; release registration must not be mistaken for independent serving qualification (TB-011, T-052, T-054). These are unresolved PR-specific contracts, not evidence of missing controls or a clearance of the changes.
